name: organs_at_risk
description: Identify normal tissues with high expression of target genes — toxicity risk for theranostics and radioligand therapy. Downloads baseline expression from EBI Expression Atlas (HPA RNA-seq, 29 human tissues), compares each gene's normal tissue expression against the target tissue, and flags organs where expression exceeds 50% of the target. Weights high-risk organs (CNS, bone marrow, heart, liver, kidney) 3x. Returns a 0-1 risk score where lower means fewer organs at risk (better safety profile).

name: analyze_table_with_python
description: Run LLM-generated Python code over the session's AIRA tables for open-ended analysis (joins, aggregations, statistical tests, plots). Two-step UX by default: submit code with approve=false to PROPOSE — the tool's response includes the code echoed back AND a markdown schema preview of every session table (row counts, columns, JSON-encoded-column hints, sample rows). Read the preview before resubmitting to verify column names, detect JSON-encoded fields, and pick correct join keys. Resubmit with approve=true to EXECUTE; auto_approve=true skips PROPOSE for trusted/short ops. Every non-underscore-prefixed table in the session is auto-injected as a pandas DataFrame named df_<table_name>; the chained predecessor is also available as `df`. Code must assign `result`. Three valid result shapes: (1) list-of-dicts or pandas DataFrame -> next chainable AIRA table; (2) base64-encoded image bytes prefixed with 'PNG_B64:' / 'PDF_B64:' / 'JPEG_B64:' -> written to /storage/localfile/, output is a one-row table with chart_url column; (3) scalar (str/int/float) -> one-row, one-column table. If the analysis result is intended for inspection only (e.g. discovery: print column names, peek at a few rows), assign a short string to `result` — it lands in the chat, not as a chainable table. AST-sandboxed via TU's python_code_executor (forbids os/subprocess/socket/urllib/requests/http/open/eval/exec by default). Pass `allowed_imports=[...]` to extend the whitelist for this call; `dependencies=[...]` to pip-install missing packages at runtime. Use whenever the user asks an analysis question that doesn't fit the deterministic SR tools — joins, aggregations, plots, custom statistics. Always pass the user's literal `code` string in `params`; `code` is required and must be forwarded verbatim. When uncertain about table shape (column names, JSON-encoded fields, asymmetric join keys across tables), do a discovery pass first: submit short code that returns a string summary of `df_<name>.columns` / `df_<name>.head(2)` for the relevant tables, then write the analysis with the actual schema in hand.

approve.description: Default false. Submit with approve=false first to PROPOSE the code; user reviews; resubmit with approve=true to EXECUTE.

dependencies.description: Optional. Comma-separated list of pip packages to install at runtime if missing (e.g. 'lifelines,plotly'). Auto-install is ON by default.
